summary: The starter prompt gives a clear goal (Python FastAPI + Beanie consent store with append-only history, TTL index, and three endpoints) and the run-environment constraints supply the target cluster and DB name. Several implementation details are unspecified (Python version, driver versions, exact routes/payloads, seed script, pinned deps, README, tests, index parameters), so a builder can start but will make concrete defaults for those gaps.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "build a Python FastAPI service using Beanie ODM that stores customer consent records and channel preferences... append-only consent history sub-array for audit... expose endpoints to record consent, withdraw consent, and retrieve the current preference state."
rubric.note: Prompt clearly states the business goal and what the sample demonstrates.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement a normal code sample (no agent orchestration) — a standalone FastAPI service that talks to DocumentDB directly.
rubric.note: Prompt references a 'DocumentDB skill' but does not state an agent framework; no agent skills are installed. See contradictions.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Target a modern supported Python 3.x, e.g. Python 3.11 (builder will use 3.11 or 3.10 as default).
rubric.note: Python language is specified but the exact version is not.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use the current stable Beanie from PyPI and its compatible motor/pymongo versions (install latest Beanie; let pip resolve compatible motor/pymongo).
rubric.note: ODM is specified but specific library versions or pinned deps are not.
skill.md provides the cluster details and enforces using the existing cluster and database name 'sample_customer_360_11' (M30, MongoDB 7.0 wire protocol, DiskANN, etc.).
skill.md requires reading connection string from DOCUMENTDB_URI environment variable and not writing secrets to files; use .env.example placeholders.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Customer consent records and channel preferences are modelled as Beanie ODM Document classes"; "consentVersion field and append-only consent history sub-array"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will define a Beanie Document with fields: customer_id (string, indexed), consentVersion (int), current_preferences (dict of channel->bool), history (list of events with timestamp, action, actor, channels), and retention_date (datetime) used for TTL.
rubric.note: Shape is sketched but field names, types and collection name(s) are left to the implementer; no shard key or relationships specified.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a small idempotent seed script inserting a few (3–5) representative consent documents for demonstration/testing.
rubric.note: Prompt does not mention seed data source, size, or license; skill.md only requires verification against live cluster but does not supply sample data.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "Add TTL indexes for data retention enforcement"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will create a TTL index on the retention_date field with a sensible default expireAfterSeconds (e.g. 365 days expressed in seconds, configurable via env), and add an index on customer_id for fast lookup. No vector or text indexes are required for this sample.
rubric.note: Only TTL index requirement is explicit; index parameters and any additional indexes are unspecified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "expose endpoints to record consent, withdraw consent, and retrieve the current preference state"
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will implement routes such as POST /consent (record), POST /consent/withdraw (withdraw), and GET /consent/{customer_id} (retrieve), with JSON request/response payloads documenting expected fields.
rubric.note: HTTP methods and high-level intent are stated but exact route names, request/response schemas and error handling are left to the implementer.
skill.md explicitly requires using the existing live cluster and disallows provisioning another cluster; Docker is available but a local gateway is not to be used.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will include basic run instructions (create .env from .env.example, pip install -r requirements.txt, uvicorn main:app --reload) and a small integration test that runs against the live cluster if available. Unit tests that run without a live cluster are not specified but likely omitted unless added by the implementer.
rubric.note: skill.md asks to verify against live cluster but exact commands, test harness and CI are unspecified.

rubric.found_in_prompt: "...stores customer consent records...append-only consent history...TTL indexes...endpoints to record consent, withdraw consent, and retrieve the current preference state."
rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Accept when: FastAPI service runs, Beanie models exist, endpoints perform described operations against sample_customer_360_11, TTL index created in code, and a small demo/seed shows the features.
rubric.note: No explicit acceptance criteria (tests, performance, coverage) provided; implementer will create pragmatic criteria.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Builder will avoid provisioning new cloud resources, will not commit secrets, and will focus on correctness/demo rather than production hardening or infra-as-code.
rubric.note: skill.md gives some constraints (use existing cluster, do not write secrets), but no cost or compliance constraints are listed.

rubric.assumption_if_unanswered: Use a simple layout (app/, tests/, scripts/seed.py), add requirements.txt, .env.example, README.md describing setup/run, and keep secrets out of the repo per skill.md.
rubric.note: Prompt/skill.md require not committing connection strings and suggest .env.example, but other repo conventions (README sections, naming) are not specified.

contradictions: Prompt asks to use 'the DocumentDB skill' but the installed_skills list is empty; no skill named 'DocumentDB' is available to the builder.
skill.md mandates using a .env.example and not writing the connection string to files; the prompt does not mention configuration details itself but references a skill that is missing.
questions_for_author: Which Python minor version should the sample target (e.g. 3.10 or 3.11)? This affects dependency compatibility and CI/test setup.
Do you have preferred route names and exact request/response schemas (e.g. POST /consents vs POST /consent, what fields are required) or should the implementer choose pragmatic defaults?
Should the sample include an idempotent seed script, pinned requirements.txt, unit tests (mocking the DB), and a README, or is delivering only the running service sufficient?
requirements_at_risk: A `.env.example` lists every setting with placeholder values — skill.md instructs using .env.example, so this is likely to be added, but the starter prompt itself did not require it. (skill.md partially covers this)
The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output — no embedding model is requested in the prompt, and skill.md does not provide model info; this is at risk.
The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them — not applicable to the prompt's scope and not covered.
One database client is created and reused across requests — not specified in prompt or skill.md; implementer may or may not follow this best practice.
A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data — seed script is not requested and skill.md doesn't supply sample data; at risk.
/search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails — search is not part of this prompt; at risk if the gallery expects search behavior.
Search results include the similarity score — not relevant to this sample as specified; at risk per reference requirements.
Dependencies are pinned in `requirements.txt` — not specified; implementer may include or omit pinned versions, so this is at risk.
Unit tests run without a live cluster — no test strategy is specified; at risk.
Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type — skill.md forbids provisioning new cluster; infra code is not requested and is at risk.
The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up — prompt doesn't request README; skill.md asks verification but not README content, so this is at risk.
The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name — no naming guidance in the prompt; at risk.
